# Deep-dive vs Sonnet+NCBI accuracy on SurfaceBench (Supp. Fig. S11)

<!-- BEGIN manuscript-legend (generated — edit the manuscript, not here) -->
## Figure legend — Supplementary Figure 11

*Verbatim from the manuscript. Generated by
`scripts/figures/sync_readme_legends.py` — edit the manuscript and
re-run; do not hand-edit inside these markers.*

> **Supplementary Figure 11.** For SurfaceBench proteins subjected to deep-dive analysis, the evidence-based assessment matched the soft-credit accuracy of Sonnet+NCBI triage, while the surface tiers reflected the difficulty of each case. For the 113 deep-dived SurfaceBench genes, deep-dive and Sonnet+NCBI triage calls are scored against the curated verdict under the soft-credit rule. a) Overall soft-credit accuracy. b) Accuracy split by ground-truth bucket (yes / contextual / no). Deep-dive bars are stacked by the tier assigned to correctly classified genes (palette as in Figure 5a): ground-truth-yes genes are called mostly canonical (58 of 68), contextual genes mostly likely (21 of 30 correct), and the correct non-surface calls all land in no. Sonnet+NCBI bars are the mean of three replicates (dots; error bar SEM); the deep dive was run once, so its bar has no spread. The two methods agree overall (97.3% vs 96.8%) and on ground-truth-yes genes (both 100%); the deep dive scores higher on contextual genes (96.8% vs 89.2%) and lower on non-surface genes (85.7% vs 97.6%; both misses were called low). None of these differences is significant by an exact McNemar test on paired gene-level correctness (overall p = 1.0; contextual p = 0.63; non-surface p = 0.50).
<!-- END manuscript-legend -->

On the SurfaceBench benchmark genes deep-dived so far (**n = 113 of 147**,
the intersection), the evidence-anchored deep dive matches the
Sonnet+NCBI triage's soft-credit accuracy, and its confidence tier
tracks ground-truth difficulty. Each protein's deep-dive surface call
and the Sonnet+NCBI triage call are scored against the curated
ground-truth verdict under the **soft-credit rule** — a
contextually-surface protein counts correct when called surface.

- **(a)** Overall soft-credit accuracy — deep dive vs Sonnet+NCBI.
- **(b)** Accuracy split by ground-truth bucket (yes / contextual / no).
  The deep-dive bar is **stacked by the tier** it assigned to the
  correctly-classified genes — canonical / likely (green and teal) and
  low (amber), with uncertain / no (grey), the same five-tier palette as
  Figure 5a — so its confidence composition is visible. Ground-truth-yes
  genes are called mostly canonical and likely, contextual genes mostly
  likely, and all 12 correct not-surface calls land in `no` (no gene in
  this set is tiered `uncertain`). Sonnet+NCBI accuracy is the
  **mean of three mainbench replicates** (one dot per replicate; error
  bar = SEM across replicates); the deep dive runs once per gene.

Deep dive and Sonnet are near-identical overall (**97.3% vs 96.8%**,
Sonnet as the replicate mean). By bucket they tie on `yes` (100% each);
the deep dive is ahead on `contextual` (96.8% vs 89.2% ± 2.2 SEM) and
Sonnet is ahead on `no` (97.6% ± 2.4 vs 85.7%). Each gap is about two
genes: the deep dive's only errors are one contextual gene called `no`
(PMEL) and two `no` genes called `low` (ATG9A, RPN1), while Sonnet misses
2–4 contextual genes per replicate and at most one `no` gene.

> Computed over the 113 benchmark genes that carry both a Sonnet verdict
> and a published deep-dive record (68 `yes`, 31 `contextual`, 14 `no`).
> The `no` bucket is the smallest, so per-bucket differences there carry
> the widest error bars.

## Reproduce

```bash
uv run make_deep_dive_vs_sonnet_benchmark.py
```

The script reads the bundled `deep_dive_vs_sonnet_benchmark.tsv` (one row
per deep-dived bench gene, carrying both predictors' soft-credit
correctness, the deep-dive tier, and the three Sonnet replicate flags)
and writes `deep_dive_vs_sonnet_benchmark.{pdf,png}`. No network access —
the data is bundled in this gist.
